results.note: Page: 'The Yurok Tribe is currently the largest Tribe in California, with more than 5,000 enrolled members.' Evidence verbatim.
Evidence verbatim, but the page dates the conveyance to June 30, 2026 (July 28, 2026 is the announcement dateline); land is on Prairie Creek. Corrected the date.
results.text: On June 30, 2026, Save the Redwoods League conveyed 125 acres on Prairie Creek, in the heart of Yurok ancestral territory, back to the Yurok Tribe.
results.evidence: transferred 125 acres of land in the heart of Yurok ancestral territory

results.note: Page: 'When we refer to ourselves we say Oohl, meaning Indian people.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'The Karuk Tribe is one of the largest Native American tribes in California' with 'ancestral lands along the Klamath River'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'Offering instruction for all ages through community classes, school partnerships, and immersion opportunities' and 'Connecting learners with fluent speakers'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: opened September 2002; museum, library, basketweaving classroom, Karuk Language Program Office; address in Happy Camp. Evidence verbatim.

Evidence verbatim (Fisheries Management Division 'charged with enumeration of harvest and escapement of anadromous fish'); species (Chinook, coho, steelhead, sturgeon, shad, lamprey) listed in the FY2019 goal statement. Page does not call the staff scientists, so that word was removed.
results.text: The Hoopa Valley Tribe runs its own Fisheries Department, which counts the harvest and spawning returns of salmon, steelhead, sturgeon and lamprey.
results.evidence: charged with enumeration of harvest and escapement of anadromous fish

results.note: Page: 'Significant progress has been made in FY 2015-2018 in restoration of lower portions of Supply and Mill creeks.' Evidence verbatim.
BIA (Indian Affairs, US Dept of the Interior) press release dated March 13, 1974: 'The valley was created by the Trinity River, the focus of reservation life.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'sponsored the formation of the Tolowa Dee-ni' Language program in 1969' and 'Language revitalization is vital for preserving Tolowa identity'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'in 1983, The Tolowa Dee-ni' Nation was restored through the Tillie Hartwick case.' and 'The restored government provided citizenship for all Taa-laa-wa Dee-ni'.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'The Nation was established in 1908 and was the largest Rancheria in the State of California, consisting of 160 acres.' Evidence verbatim.
Sonoma County Regional Parks: 'The 688-acre Kashia Coastal Reserve straddles both sides of Highway 1', 'immediately north of Salt Point State Park'; owned by the Kashia Band. Evidence verbatim.
Page: approximately 860 members; Tribal Government Office located in Santa Rosa, California. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'lands that extended from the Gualala River in the North to Duncan's Point south of the Russian River.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: federation of Coast Miwok and Southern Pomo groups; 'On December 27, 2000, President Clinton signed into law legislation restoring federal recognition'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'The Tribe purchases approximately 254 acres of land for its reservation just outside of Rohnert Park'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'launch its own Tribal TANF program for low-income Native American families in Sonoma and Marin counties'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: Rancheria purchased October 26, 1910; original acquisition 289.52 acres; 'Today, there are over 1,700 fee and trust land acres.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'Today, the Me-Wuk culture is alive and still widely practiced.' and 'The Acorn Festival, established in October 1966'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'In January 2005, the Tribe opened the Tuolumne Me-Wuk Indian Health Center.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: Culture Department 'established the Language Program in 2008'; photo caption 'The official unveiling of the Samala-English Dictionary.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'Established on December 27, 1901', 'the original 99-acre Santa Ynez Reservation', growth 'to more than 1,500 acres'. Evidence verbatim.
Evidence verbatim, but the page does not describe the tomol as a plank canoe or say the crossing is on the ocean. Replaced the unsupported clause with what the same sentence says.
results.text: Tribal members take part in a historic tomol crossing each year, and the Tribe hosts the annual Chumash Inter-Tribal Pow-Wow and Chumash Culture Day.
results.evidence: We also participate in a historic tomol crossing each year

results.note: Evidence verbatim ('Huhuunga ... is a one-acre parcel in Altadena that was returned to Tongva stewardship in 2022'), but the page does not say TTPC cares for it; it says the parcel 'currently serves as the home of TTPC'. Corrected.
results.text: In 2022 Huhuunga, a one-acre parcel in Altadena, was returned to Tongva stewardship. It is now home to the Tongva-led Tongva Taraxat Paxaavxa Conservancy.
results.evidence: one-acre parcel in Altadena that was returned to Tongva stewardship

results.note: Page: 'TTPC serves Tongva people, the Native community, the Indigenous diaspora, and kuuyam (guests)'; describes itself as a Tongva-led 501(c)(3) nonprofit, not a tribal authority or governmental body. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'The Viejas Government is founded on a participatory democracy'; 'Tribal government officials are elected to four-year terms of office by the general council'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'not only in San Diego, but also with our Kumeyaay brothers and sisters in Baja Norte.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'The Cahuilla Band of Indians are Mountain Cahuilla (Qawishpa Cahuillangnah)'. Evidence verbatim.
History page: 'their traditional territory covers a large area in Riverside and San Diego counties'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'We are sovereign nation rooted in culture and tradition' and Mission 'perpetuating our culture through strong governance'. Evidence verbatim.
Evidence verbatim and 1865 confirmed ('Established in 1865, the Morongo Indian Reservation was one of nine small reservations'), but the page does not mention Cahuilla territory. Removed that clause.
results.text: Established in 1865, the Morongo Indian Reservation now spans more than 35,000 acres.
results.evidence: the Morongo Indian Reservation spans more than 35,000 acres

results.note: Page: 'Morongo provides essential services through an independent tribal government.' and 'Tribal Members elect a seven-member Tribal Council'. Evidence verbatim.

NMAI American Indian magazine, Summer 2019: 'They teach the language to adults and youth in classes held Mondays through Thursdays.'; Eagle's Nest immersion classes in the tribe's Head Start. Evidence verbatim.
USFS: 'Da ow ga, the Washoe word for "lake" is thought to be the source for "Tahoe."' Hedge preserved. Evidence verbatim.
USFS: 'the Washoe Tribe and their ancestors had been calling the resource-rich Lake Tahoe their home for at least 2,000 years.' Evidence verbatim.

Page: 'The Te-Moak Tribe is comprised of four Bands:' Battle Mountain Band, Elko Band Colony, South Fork Reservation, Wells Band Colony; 'Tribal Elections are held every three years.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'descendants of an ancient widespread people whose name is "Newe" meaning "The People."' Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'The traditional Western Shoshone territory covered southern Idaho, the central part of Nevada,' plus NW Utah and the Death Valley region. Evidence verbatim.

The evidence phrase is verbatim but describes where a webcam is 'Perched at Furnace Creek'; the page never says the Timbisha live at Furnace Creek. It does say 'The Timbisha people, part of the larger Western Shoshone group, have lived in this region for thousands of years' (region = Death Valley and its surrounding areas in California and Nevada) and that the Timbisha Shoshone Village is in Death Valley National Park. Rewrote text and evidence.
results.text: The Timbisha, part of the larger Western Shoshone people, have lived in Death Valley and its surrounding areas for thousands of years, and their village sits inside Death Valley National Park.
results.evidence: part of the larger Western Shoshone group, have lived in this region

results.note: Page: 'a federally recognized Native American tribe'; 'Today, the tribe continues to preserve its language, traditions, and sovereignty while advocating for its rights.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'approximately 3,014 (as of May 2024) enrolled members'; 'governed by ten Tribal Council members'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'The area of the reservation contains 475,000 acres or 742.2 square miles.'; 'Pyramid Lake is approximately 27 miles long and 11 miles wide at its largest width.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'The Language Program offers community language classes, in-school language instruction,' plus meetings with fluent speakers; Paiute language named. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'a federally recognized tribe in north-central Idaho with more than 3,500 enrolled citizens.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'Headquartered in Lapwai, ID, the Nez Perce Reservation spans about 770,000 acres.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'The Nimipuutímt language is an integral part of Nez Perce culture.' Spelling Nimipuutímt confirmed. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'teaching the languages of Umatilla, Walla Walla and Weyíiletpuu (Cayuse) to all ages.' and 'By tapping into the knowledge of our fluent speakers'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'Language for the people of Nixyáawii, the place of many springs, is a way of life and being.' Evidence verbatim.

Page: 'A key accomplishment in natural resources is the restoration of salmon to the Umatilla river after 70 years of extinction.' Presented as a CTUIR accomplishment on the Tribes' own history page. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'Located in southwestern Washington State is the 1,130,000 acres reservation'. Evidence verbatim.

Evidence verbatim ('arcing around Mount Adams are fourteen gold stars and fourteen eagle feathers honoring the bands of the Yakama nation'), but the page calls it the Yakama Nation flag, not an emblem. Corrected.
results.text: Arcing around Mount Adams on the Yakama Nation flag are fourteen gold stars and fourteen eagle feathers honoring its bands.
results.evidence: fourteen gold stars and fourteen eagle feathers honoring the bands

results.note: Page: daily Ichishkíin word; 'This daily practice is essential for maintaining language fluency'; 'The Ichishkiin language, also known as Sahaptin, is a vital part of the cultural heritage of the Yakama Nation.' Evidence verbatim.
Museum page heading 'Three tribes share their history and culture'; greetings in Ichishkiin, Numu (Paiute) and Kiksht (Wasco); copyright The Confederated Tribes of Warm Springs. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'In 1937, the three tribes organized as the Confederated Tribes of the Warm Springs Reservation of Oregon', adopting a constitution and bylaws. Evidence verbatim.

Evidence verbatim ('The tribes also kept their rights to harvest fish, game and other foods', 'in their usual and accustomed places'), but the page names only the Warm Springs and Wasco tribes as 1855 treaty parties; Paiute settlement on the reservation began in 1879. 'Their 1855 treaty the tribes' on a three-tribe card implied the Paiute too. Corrected.
results.text: Under the 1855 treaty, the Warm Springs and Wasco tribes kept their rights to harvest fish, game and other foods in their usual and accustomed places.
results.evidence: kept their rights to harvest fish, game and other foods

results.note: NWIC: 'main campus located on the Lummi Indian Reservation in Washington State'; 'the only accredited Tribal College serving the states of Washington, Oregon, and Idaho.' Evidence verbatim.
NWIC: 'grew from the Lummi Indian School of Aquaculture, founded in 1973'; 'In 2010, NWIC became accredited at the baccalaureate level.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'We are the Lhaq'temish, the Lummi People'; 'We are fishers, hunters, gatherers, and harvesters of nature's abundance.'; 'on the shores and waters of Puget Sound.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'Our tribal population is over 5,100 and growing, with 2,700 members residing on the 22,000 acres Tulalip Indian Reservation.' Evidence verbatim.
Vision: 'Every tribal home, every tribal workplace, every tribal gathering, and every schoolroom for tribal children will be a Lushootseed-rich environment.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'successors in interest to the Snohomish, Snoqualmie, Skykomish, and other allied tribes and bands' and 'signatory to the 1855 Treaty of Point Elliott'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'The Muckleshoot Indian Tribe has become one of South King County's largest employers, supporting 3,300 direct jobs'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'Among Puget Sound Tribes, the Muckleshoot uniquely possesses rights under two treaties:' (Point Elliott and Medicine Creek). Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'The Muckleshoot language is a dialect of Puget Salish, or Lushootseed.'; programs 'that teach our youth and keep our Native language alive.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: name puyaləpabš glossed 'people at the bend at the bottom (of the river)'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'In the late 20th century, Tribal Members fought for fishing rights, leading to the historic Boldt Decision in 1974.' Evidence verbatim.

Evidence verbatim and 'one of the most urban tribes in the United States' confirmed, but 'these waters' refers to the Puyallup River ('Living off the waters of the Puyallup River ... the Puyallup People continue to fish, hunt and travel these waters'), not Puget Sound.
results.text: One of the most urban tribes in the United States, the Puyallup still fish, hunt and travel the waters of the Puyallup River.
results.evidence: the Puyallup People continue to fish, hunt and travel these waters

results.note: Page: 'We're located on the NW tip of the Continental US'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'The name Makah was attributed to the Tribe by the neighboring tribes, meaning "people generous with food"'. Evidence verbatim.

Evidence verbatim ('In the 70's, our southernmost village was discovered'; 'artifacts from our ancestors from 300 to 500 years ago were recovered'). The page dates the ancestors 300 to 500 years ago, not 300 to 500 years before the 1970s; corrected the time reference.
results.text: When a southernmost Makah village was uncovered in the 1970s, artifacts from ancestors who lived 300 to 500 years ago were recovered.
results.evidence: artifacts from our ancestors from 300 to 500 years ago were recovered

results.note: Page: 'The 208,000-acre Quinault Indian Reservation is located on the southwestern corner of Washington's Olympic Peninsula', between the Olympic range and the Pacific. Evidence verbatim.

Page: 'The Mission of the Quinault Language Department is to revitalize the Quinault language.'; 'In-person classes are offered in Taholah, Queets and Hoquiam during Fall, Winter and Spring.' Evidence verbatim.

Evidence verbatim ('The Planning Department will be updating the Taholah Master Relocation Plan for the 2026 calendar year'), but no sentence says the village is being relocated to an upper village site; the page only references planning meetings about 'the Upper Village and potential layouts'. Softened to what the page states.
results.text: The Nation has a Taholah Village Relocation Master Plan that includes planning for an upper village, and its Planning Department is updating the plan for 2026.
results.evidence: updating the Taholah Master Relocation Plan for the 2026 calendar year

results.note: Evidence verbatim ('has been monitoring ambient air quality in partnership with EPA for more than 16 years'; analyst quote 'two major oil refineries ... right next to the reservation'). The page has no article date (only 'Last Updated on October 1, 2025' and a 2016 site copyright), so the '16 years' count cannot be anchored to as_of 2025; removed the duration. Recommend as_of null.
results.text: The Swinomish Tribe monitors air quality in partnership with the EPA, with two major oil refineries right next to its reservation.
results.evidence: monitoring ambient air quality in partnership with EPA

results.note: Evidence verbatim, but the page lists 'wind speed and direction, temperature and relative humidity, barometric pressure, solar radiation and precipitation', not rainfall. Corrected the weather list.
results.text: Swinomish monitors record real-time data on particulates, ozone and nitrogen dioxide, plus weather such as wind, temperature, humidity and precipitation.
results.evidence: records real-time continuous pollution data for particulates, ozone and nitrogen dioxide

results.note: Page: 'the most diverse confederation of Tribes and Bands on a single reservation in the United States.' Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'In 1977 our lobbying of Congress to repeal our Termination was successful'. Evidence verbatim.

Evidence verbatim ('It consists of roughly 400 pages and approximately 12,000 entries'); Talking Dictionary confirmed. The page names the dictionary 'Nuu-wee-ya'' (Our words), an Athabaskan language dictionary; 'Siletz Dee-ni' is used for separate Language Volumes 1 to 3. Corrected the name.
results.text: The Tribe's Athabaskan language dictionary, Nuu-wee-ya' (Our words), holds about 12,000 entries, and a Talking Dictionary lets learners hear words spoken aloud.

results.note: Evidence verbatim ('A nine-member Tribal Council, elected by the Tribe's voting membership, governs approximately 5,400 enrolled tribal members.'). The page says over 30 tribes and bands 'comprise' the confederation, not that members descend from them. Corrected.
results.text: A nine-member Tribal Council, elected by voting members, governs about 5,400 enrolled members of a confederation of over 30 tribes and bands.

results.note: Page: recognition 'ended on August 13, 1954'; Restoration Act signed November 22, 1983; 'Five years later ... the Tribe regained 9,811 acres of the original reservation' (Reservation Act September 9, 1988). Evidence verbatim.
Page: 'Once at risk of disappearing, Chinuk Wawa is seeing a resurgence', 'being actively taught', 'used in cultural education'. Evidence verbatim.
